title: Assessing Breathing: Pulse Oximetry and Capnography
next: Chapter 13, Lesson 3: Clearing the airway, oxygen, BVM ventilation, CPAP and PEEP

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already count respirations, read SpO₂ and listen to the chest. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize inadequate breathing before the numbers crash
  2. Know what SpO₂ can and can't tell you
  3. Read ETCO₂ numbers and waveforms to judge ventilation

Textbook: Chapter 13, PDF pages 939–966
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already count respirations, put on a pulse oximeter, and listen to lung sounds. As a PCP, your assessment has to go deeper, because your findings now decide whether you use CPAP, a PEEP valve, or a new drug. Today we cover three things. First, how to recognize inadequate breathing early, before the numbers crash. Second, what pulse oximetry can and cannot tell you. And third, end-tidal carbon dioxide, or ETCO2, the carbon dioxide at the end of each breath, measured by capnography. It's your best window into ventilation.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们已经会数呼吸、夹血氧仪、听呼吸音。作为 PCP，评估要更深入，因为现在你的发现决定要不要用 CPAP、PEEP 阀，或者一种新药。今天讲三件事：第一，怎样在数字崩掉之前及早认出呼吸不足；第二，脉搏血氧能告诉你什么、不能告诉你什么；第三，呼气末二氧化碳（ETCO2），也就是每次呼气末尾的二氧化碳，用二氧化碳描记来测。它是你观察通气最好的窗口。

slides.title: Is this breathing adequate?
slides.body:
AgeNormal rate per min
Adult12–20
Child (1–18 yrs)12–37
Infant (1 mo–1 yr)30–53
  • Inadequate: shallow, noisy, confused, cyanotic
  • Tripod position; refuses to lie flat
  • Retractions, nasal flaring, pursed lips, neck muscles
  • One side rises less: less air into that lung
slides.say: Start with what you know, but use it like a PCP. Normal adult rates are twelve to twenty a minute; children one to eighteen years, twelve to thirty-seven; infants, thirty to fifty-three. Signs of inadequate breathing include shallow breaths, abnormal breath sounds, altered mental status, and cyanosis. Look at the position: the tripod position, leaning forward on the arms, and refusing to lie flat. Look for retractions, skin pulling in between the ribs or above the collarbones, plus nasal flaring, pursed lips, and neck muscles working. If one side rises less, less air is entering that lung. If breathing is inadequate, start positive-pressure ventilation with high-concentration oxygen right away.
slides.sayZh: 先从你熟悉的说起，但要用 PCP 的方式来用。正常呼吸频率：成人每分钟十二到二十次；一到十八岁儿童十二到三十七次；婴儿三十到五十三次。呼吸不足的征象包括：呼吸浅、异常呼吸音、意识改变和发绀。看体位：三脚架位，也就是前倾撑着手臂，以及拒绝平躺。看有没有三凹征，也就是肋间或锁骨上方的皮肤往里陷，还有鼻翼扇动、缩唇呼吸、颈部肌肉用力。如果一侧起伏较小，说明进入那侧肺的空气少。一旦呼吸不足，马上开始正压通气，加高浓度氧。

slides.title: Patterns and red flags
slides.body:
PatternPoints to
Kussmaul: deep and fastDiabetic ketoacidosis
Cheyne-Stokes: up, down, pauseWorrying with brain injury
Biot: irregular, with pausesRaised intracranial pressure
Apneustic: long gasp inBrainstem injury
Agonal: slow, irregular gaspsBrain anoxia; treat as no breathing

Pulsus paradoxus: systolic falls > 10 mmHg on inhaling. Ever in ICU or intubated for this?
slides.say: Some breathing patterns point to a cause. Kussmaul breathing is deep and fast; think diabetic ketoacidosis. Cheyne-Stokes rises and falls, then pauses; it isn't ominous unless it's extreme or there's a brain injury. Biot breathing is irregular with pauses and suggests rising pressure inside the skull. Apneustic breathing, long gasps in with very short breaths out, points to the brainstem. Agonal breaths are slow gasps from a brain without oxygen; treat them as no breathing. Pulsus paradoxus means the systolic pressure drops more than ten millimetres of mercury when the patient breathes in, as in severe asthma or tension pneumothorax. And always ask: have you ever been in intensive care or intubated for this? A yes means this patient can crash fast.
slides.sayZh: 有些呼吸型态能指向病因。Kussmaul 呼吸又深又快，想到糖尿病酮症酸中毒。陈-施呼吸渐强渐弱、然后暂停；除非非常极端或有脑外伤，否则不算凶兆。Biot 呼吸不规则、带暂停，提示颅内压升高。长吸式呼吸是长长的吸气、极短的呼气，指向脑干。濒死呼吸是缓慢的喘息，来自缺氧的大脑，要按没有呼吸处理。奇脉是指病人吸气时收缩压下降超过十毫米汞柱，见于重度哮喘或张力性气胸。还要一定问：你有没有因为这个病进过 ICU 或插过管？回答是的话，这个病人可能很快恶化。

slides.q: You arrive to find a known diabetic who is drowsy and breathing deeply and rapidly. What is the best interpretation?
options: Kussmaul breathing: the body is blowing off acid, likely diabetic ketoacidosis
Cheyne-Stokes breathing: normal during sleep, no concern
Anxiety hyperventilation: coach the patient to slow down
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. You arrive to find a known diabetic who is drowsy and breathing deeply and rapidly. What is the best interpretation? A, Kussmaul breathing: the body is blowing off acid, likely diabetic ketoacidosis. B, Cheyne-Stokes breathing: normal during sleep, no concern. C, anxiety hyperventilation: coach the patient to slow down. D, apneustic breathing: a brainstem injury. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。你到场发现一名已知糖尿病病人昏昏欲睡，呼吸又深又快。最合理的解读是什么？A，Kussmaul 呼吸：身体在排酸，很可能是糖尿病酮症酸中毒；B，陈-施呼吸：睡眠中正常，不用担心；C，焦虑性过度通气：引导病人放慢呼吸；D，长吸式呼吸：脑干损伤。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. Deep, rapid breathing in a diabetic is Kussmaul breathing: the body blows off carbon dioxide to make up for acidosis. B is wrong because Cheyne-Stokes rises and falls with pauses, and a drowsy patient is never a case of no concern. C is dangerous: this fast breathing is compensation, so don't try to slow it. D describes long gasps in with very short breaths out, which is not what you see here.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。糖尿病病人又深又快的呼吸是 Kussmaul 呼吸：身体通过排出二氧化碳来代偿酸中毒。B 错，陈-施呼吸是渐强渐弱带暂停，而且昏昏欲睡的病人绝不是「不用担心」。C 很危险：这种快呼吸是代偿，不要去压它。D 描述的是长吸气、极短呼气，与这里看到的不符。

slides.title: Pulse oximetry: what it tells you
slides.body:
• % of hemoglobin carrying O₂ (SpO₂)
  • Normal > 95%; < 95% in a non-smoker suggests hypoxemia
  • < 90% with distress: aggressive oxygen
  • Check: displayed pulse = palpated radial pulse
  • Best for trends: falling SpO₂ in trauma, find the cause
  • BC: titrate O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%; record SpO₂ changes
slides.say: The pulse oximeter shines light through a finger or earlobe and estimates the percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen. It also shows a pulse rate; compare it with the radial pulse you feel. If they don't match, don't trust the reading. Normal is above ninety-five percent. Below ninety-five in a non-smoker suggests hypoxemia, and below ninety with respiratory distress calls for aggressive oxygen. The oximeter is best for trends. In trauma, a slowly falling saturation may be your first clue to a developing tension pneumothorax. In BC, the target in most protocols is a saturation of ninety-four percent or higher, and you record how it changes with each treatment.
slides.sayZh: 脉搏血氧仪让光穿过手指或耳垂，估算携带氧气的血红蛋白占多少百分比。它同时显示脉率，要和你摸到的桡动脉脉搏对一对，对不上就别信读数。正常高于百分之九十五；非吸烟者低于九十五提示低氧血症；低于九十并伴呼吸窘迫，就要积极给氧。血氧仪最擅长看趋势：创伤时血氧慢慢往下掉，可能是张力性气胸正在形成的第一条线索。在 BC，大多数流程的目标是血氧百分之九十四以上，并记录每次处理后的变化。

slides.title: When SpO₂ lies
slides.body:
• Carbon monoxide or methemoglobin: normal number, hypoxic patient
  • Poor perfusion (shock, cold, arrest): try the earlobe
  • Bright light, movement, nail polish
  • It shows oxygenation, not ventilation

Blue and struggling? Believe the patient.
slides.say: Now the weak spots. In carbon monoxide poisoning, the oximeter can't tell carbon monoxide from oxygen on the hemoglobin, so it may show a normal number in a badly hypoxic patient. Methemoglobin, an abnormal form of hemoglobin, does the same; a special CO-oximeter can measure them separately. Poor perfusion from shock, cold, or cardiac arrest gives a weak or absent reading, so try the earlobe. Bright light, movement and nail polish also cause errors. Most important, the oximeter shows oxygenation, not ventilation. On high-flow oxygen, the saturation can stay high while carbon dioxide climbs. So if the patient is blue and struggling, believe the patient, not the number.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲它的弱点。一氧化碳中毒时，血氧仪分不清血红蛋白上挂的是一氧化碳还是氧，所以病人严重缺氧，读数却可能正常。高铁血红蛋白，一种异常的血红蛋白，也会这样；专门的 CO 血氧仪可以分别测出来。休克、寒冷或心脏骤停造成灌注差，读数会变弱甚至没有，可以改夹耳垂。强光、活动和指甲油也会造成误差。最重要的是：血氧仪反映的是氧合，不是通气。吸着高流量氧时，血氧可以一直很高，二氧化碳却在上升。所以如果病人发紫、拼命喘，相信病人，别信数字。

slides.title: Blood gases: the full picture
slides.body:
ValueNormalTells you about
pH7.35–7.45acid–base
HCO₃⁻21–28 mEq/Lacid–base
PaCO₂35–45 mmHgventilation
PaO₂80–100 mmHgoxygenation

On scene: SpO₂ stands in for oxygenation, ETCO₂ for ventilation. Peak flow in asthma: best of 3.
slides.say: Paramedics don't usually draw arterial blood gases, but the numbers help you think. pH, normally seven point three five to seven point four five, and bicarbonate, twenty-one to twenty-eight, describe acid and base. PaCO2, the carbon dioxide pressure in arterial blood, normally thirty-five to forty-five millimetres of mercury, describes ventilation. PaO2, normally eighty to one hundred, describes oxygenation. That split is the key idea today. On scene, the pulse oximeter stands in for oxygenation, and capnography stands in for ventilation. For asthma, peak expiratory flow helps: seat the patient, have them blow as hard as they can three times, and take the best. A rising number means treatment is working.
slides.sayZh: 院前一般不抽动脉血气，但这些数字能帮你思考。pH 正常七点三五到七点四五，碳酸氢根二十一到二十八，反映酸碱平衡。PaCO2 是动脉血里的二氧化碳分压，正常三十五到四十五毫米汞柱，反映通气。PaO2 正常八十到一百，反映氧合。这个分工就是今天的核心。在现场，脉搏血氧代表氧合，二氧化碳描记代表通气。哮喘可以测呼气峰流速：让病人坐好，尽全力吹三次，取最好的一次；数值上升说明治疗有效。

slides.title: ETCO₂: the exhaust of metabolism
slides.body:
Cells burn O₂→blood carries CO₂ to lungs→breathed out and measured
  • Normal ETCO₂ about 35–45 mmHg, 2–5 below PaCO₂
  • Colorimetric: purple to yellow; a spot check only
  • Capnometer: number. Capnograph: number + waveform
  • Breathing patient: special nasal cannula sampling line
slides.say: Carbon dioxide is like the exhaust of a car engine. As long as cells burn oxygen and blood carries the result to the lungs, carbon dioxide comes out with each breath. End-tidal carbon dioxide is the amount at the very end of a breath, and it closely tracks the arterial level: normally thirty-five to forty-five millimetres of mercury, usually two to five lower than the PaCO2. A colorimetric detector turns from purple to yellow when carbon dioxide is present; it's only a quick spot check. A capnometer gives a number. A capnograph gives a number and a waveform. And you don't need a tube: a breathing patient can wear a special nasal cannula with a sampling line.
slides.sayZh: 二氧化碳就像汽车发动机的尾气：只要细胞在烧氧、血液把产物运到肺，每次呼气就会排出二氧化碳。呼气末二氧化碳是一口气最末尾的含量，它和动脉血里的水平很接近：正常三十五到四十五毫米汞柱，通常比 PaCO2 低二到五。比色检测器遇到二氧化碳从紫色变黄色，只能快速点检；二氧化碳测定仪给你一个数字；二氧化碳描记仪给你数字加波形。而且不一定要有导管：自主呼吸的病人可以戴一种带采样管的专用鼻导管。

slides.title: Reading the waveform
slides.body:
What you seeThink
Square boxes, 35–45Normal
Tall (> 45), far apartHypoventilation, e.g. opioids
Small (< 35), close togetherHyperventilation, e.g. anxiety
Sloped "shark fin"Bronchospasm: asthma, COPD
Baseline above zeroRebreathing CO₂
slides.say: A normal waveform looks like a row of boxes. It starts flat at zero, rises sharply as the patient breathes out, runs along a plateau of alveolar gas, and drops back to zero as they breathe in. The top of the plateau is the ETCO2 number. Now the abnormal shapes. Tall waves above forty-five, far apart, mean hypoventilation: carbon dioxide is building up, as in an opioid overdose. Small waves below thirty-five, close together, mean hyperventilation, as in anxiety, metabolic acidosis, head injury or pulmonary embolism. A sloped shark-fin shape means bronchospasm: the alveoli can't empty, as in asthma or COPD. If the baseline never returns to zero, the patient is rebreathing carbon dioxide.
slides.sayZh: 正常波形像一排方盒子：从零的平线开始，病人呼气时急剧上升，沿着一段肺泡气的平台走，病人吸气时再落回零。平台的最高点就是 ETCO2 数值。再看异常形状：波很高、超过四十五、间隔很远，是通气不足，二氧化碳在堆积，比如阿片类过量。波很小、低于三十五、挨得很近，是过度通气，见于焦虑、代谢性酸中毒、颅脑外伤或肺栓塞。斜着上升的鲨鱼鳍形状是支气管痉挛：肺泡排不空，比如哮喘或 COPD。如果基线始终回不到零，说明病人在重复吸入二氧化碳。

slides.q: After an opioid overdose, your patient is on a non-rebreather. SpO₂ 97%, RR 7 and shallow, ETCO₂ 62 mmHg with tall waves. Best action?
options: Nothing: the SpO₂ is normal, so breathing is adequate
Turn up the oxygen and recheck in 10 minutes
Assist ventilation with a BVM and watch the ETCO₂ come down
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. After an opioid overdose, your patient is on a non-rebreather. The saturation is ninety-seven percent, the rate is seven and shallow, and the ETCO2 is sixty-two with tall waves. What is the best action? A, nothing: the saturation is normal, so breathing is adequate. B, turn up the oxygen and recheck in ten minutes. C, assist ventilation with a BVM and watch the ETCO2 come down. D, apply CPAP to improve oxygenation. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。阿片类过量后，病人戴着非重复呼吸面罩，血氧百分之九十七，呼吸每分钟七次且很浅，ETCO2 六十二，波形很高。最好的处理是什么？A，什么都不做：血氧正常，说明呼吸足够；B，把氧开大，十分钟后再查；C，用 BVM 辅助通气，看着 ETCO2 降下来；D，上 CPAP 改善氧合。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. The saturation looks fine only because of the high-flow oxygen. The slow rate and an ETCO2 of sixty-two show hypoventilation: carbon dioxide is building up. The fix is to ventilate with a BVM, and good ventilation should bring the ETCO2 back toward thirty-five to forty-five. A trusts the oximeter for something it can't measure. B adds oxygen to a ventilation problem. D is wrong because BC lists hypoventilation as a contraindication to CPAP.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。血氧看起来正常只是因为在吸高流量氧；呼吸慢、ETCO2 六十二，说明通气不足，二氧化碳在堆积。解决办法是用 BVM 通气，通气做好了，ETCO2 应该回到三十五到四十五左右。A 用血氧仪去判断它测不了的东西；B 给通气问题加氧；D 错，因为 BC 把通气不足列为 CPAP 的禁忌证。

slides.title: ETCO₂ going up or down
slides.body:
PatientETCO₂ upETCO₂ down
BreathingHypoventilationHyperventilation
Apneic, has pulseBagging too slowBagging too fast
Cardiac arrestSudden, sustained rise: ROSCWeak CPR, long arrest

Flat line with an advanced airway: think tube out (or a blocked sampling line).
slides.say: ETCO2 also helps you adjust your own care. In a breathing patient, a rising number means hypoventilation and a falling number means hyperventilation. In an apneic patient you're bagging, a high number means you're too slow, and a low number means too fast. In cardiac arrest, a low number may mean compressions aren't deep or fast enough, or that the arrest has been long. A sudden, sustained jump, often above forty, suggests return of spontaneous circulation, or ROSC. With an advanced airway, a sudden flat line means the tube may be out, though a blocked sampling line can do the same. Intubation itself isn't on the BC PCP licensing exam.
slides.sayZh: ETCO2 还能帮你调整自己的操作。自主呼吸的病人，数字升高是通气不足，下降是过度通气。你在捏球的无自主呼吸病人，数字高说明你太慢，数字低说明太快。心脏骤停时，数字低可能是按压深度或频率不够，或者骤停时间已经很长；突然持续跳高，常常超过四十，提示自主循环恢复，也就是 ROSC。有高级气道时，突然变成一条平线说明导管可能脱出了，不过采样管堵住也会这样。气管插管本身不在 BC PCP 执照考试范围内。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: SOB with asthma / COPD
slides.body:
BC protocol: shortness of breath with a history of asthma/COPD

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Sit up, leaning forward; limit movement
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94% (may not be achievable)
  • Auscultate; salbutamol by nebulizer or MDI

PCP adds

  • Salbutamol with ipratropium (ipratropium once)
  • IM epinephrine if SpO₂ < 90% and/or spasm unresolved
  • Consider dexamethasone and CPAP
slides.say: Here's where better assessment pays off. In the BC protocol for shortness of breath with asthma or COPD, the left column is what you already do: sit the patient up, leaning forward, limit movement, give oxygen aiming for ninety-four percent, though it may not be reachable, listen to the chest, take a history and vitals, and give salbutamol by nebulizer or inhaler. The right column is new. The PCP can add ipratropium to the salbutamol, given only once. If the saturation is under ninety percent, or bronchospasm stays moderate to severe despite salbutamol, the PCP considers intramuscular epinephrine. The PCP also considers dexamethasone and CPAP. Every one of these decisions depends on your numbers and your stethoscope.
slides.sayZh: 更好的评估在这里就派上用场了。在 BC 哮喘或 COPD 伴气促的流程里，左栏是你本来就做的：让病人坐起、身体前倾，限制活动；给氧目标百分之九十四，不过可能达不到；听诊；问病史、测生命体征；用雾化或吸入器给沙丁胺醇。右栏是新的：PCP 可以在沙丁胺醇里加异丙托溴铵，只给一次；如果血氧低于百分之九十，或者用了沙丁胺醇后支气管痉挛仍是中到重度，PCP 考虑肌注肾上腺素；PCP 还会考虑地塞米松和 CPAP。每一个决定都取决于你的数字和你的听诊器。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Normal SpO₂ on high-flow O₂ can hide CO₂ build-up
  • Never treat a number alone: recheck probe, pulse, patient
  • Long cardiac arrest: ETCO₂ can be very low; read in context
  • Reassess after every treatment and record the change
  • Past ICU or intubation: expect rapid deterioration
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch out for. First, a normal saturation on high-flow oxygen can hide carbon dioxide building up. Watch rate, depth and mental status. Second, never treat a number alone. If a reading doesn't fit the patient, recheck the probe, the pulse and the patient. Third, after a long cardiac arrest, ETCO2 can be very low because little carbon dioxide reaches the lungs, so read it in context. Fourth, as a PCP you'll give more treatments, so reassess after every one and record how the numbers change. And finally, a patient who has been in intensive care or intubated for this problem before can deteriorate fast, so plan ahead.
slides.sayZh: 这些是新的注意事项。第一，高流量氧下血氧正常，可能掩盖二氧化碳堆积；要盯着呼吸频率、深度和神志。第二，永远不要只治疗一个数字；读数和病人对不上时，重新检查探头、脉搏和病人本身。第三，骤停时间长了，回到肺里的二氧化碳很少，ETCO2 可能很低，要结合情况看。第四，作为 PCP 你给的处理更多了，每一次都要复评，并记录数字的变化。最后，以前因为这个病进过 ICU 或插过管的病人可能恶化得很快，要提前准备。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Lung sounds: at least 6 points on the front or 6 on the back
  • Pain history: BC accepts OPQRRRST or LOTARP, used in full
  • SpO₂ target in BC protocols: ≥ 94%
  • CPAP (PCP): RR > 24 + SpO₂ < 94% on O₂ + accessory muscles

The book suggests CPAP when SpO₂ < 90%; on the BC exam, use the BC criteria.
slides.say: A few BC points for the exam. When you listen to the lungs, BC expects at least six points on the front or six on the back; the textbook only says to compare side to side, front and back. For pain, BC scoring expects either the OPQRRRST or the LOTARP memory aid, and using only part of one costs marks, so practise one fully. In the BC protocols, your oxygen target is a saturation of ninety-four percent or higher. And one PCP difference: the textbook suggests CPAP when the saturation is below ninety percent, but the BC CPAP guideline uses different triggers: a rate above twenty-four, a saturation under ninety-four percent while on oxygen, and accessory muscle use, all together.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考试要点。听肺部时，BC 要求前胸至少六个点或后背六个点；教材只说要左右对比、前后都听。问疼痛时，BC 评分要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 其中一个口诀，只用一部分会扣分，所以要把其中一个练完整。BC 流程里给氧目标是血氧百分之九十四以上。还有一个 PCP 的差异：教材建议血氧低于百分之九十时用 CPAP，但 BC 的 CPAP 指南用的是另一套触发条件：呼吸频率超过二十四、吸氧状态下血氧低于九十四、使用辅助呼吸肌，三条同时满足。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Inadequate breathing: rate, depth, effort, mental status
  2. SpO₂ = oxygenation; ETCO₂ = ventilation (35–45 mmHg)
  3. Your findings now trigger PCP tools: ipratropium, IM epi, CPAP

Next: clearing the airway, oxygen, BVM, CPAP and PEEP
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: inadequate breathing shows in the rate, the depth, the effort and the mental status, not just in the saturation. Two: the pulse oximeter tells you about oxygenation; ETCO2 tells you about ventilation, normally thirty-five to forty-five. Three: as a PCP, your findings now trigger new treatments, like ipratropium, intramuscular epinephrine and CPAP, so your assessment has to be precise. Next lesson, we put it all into action: clearing the airway, oxygen devices, BVM ventilation, and the PCP's two pressure tools, CPAP and PEEP. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，呼吸不足体现在频率、深度、费力程度和神志上，不只是血氧。二，脉搏血氧告诉你氧合，ETCO2 告诉你通气，正常三十五到四十五。三，作为 PCP，你的发现现在会触发新的处理，比如异丙托溴铵、肌注肾上腺素和 CPAP，所以评估必须精准。下节课我们把这些用到实践中：清理气道、给氧装置、BVM 通气，以及 PCP 的两样压力工具 CPAP 和 PEEP。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
